xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2602: feat(pipeline): union in-pipeline signal + bead↔issue state fidelity (visibility gap + orphaned-bead leak)

plan.title: feat(pipeline): union in-pipeline signal + bead↔issue state fidelity (visibility gap + orphaned-bead leak)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: The Command Deck issue tree only shows issues with a live registered pipeline agent, so real in-flight work falls off the view: handoff/bypass conversations carry no issueId (PAN-2564 implemented by a conversation on bypass/pan-2564 was invisible), and work that lives in artifacts (branch ahead of main, open PR, partial beads) with no running agent is excluded by design at resource-discovery.ts:661-712. Separately, 36 GitHub-closed issues carry orphaned open beads because nothing reconciles beads when an issue goes terminal, which makes raw bead-progress ~95% noise and leaks state fidelity.
narratives.Proposal: Extend computeResourceAllocatedIssues() with a union of cheap, cached work-artifact signals (branch/bypass ahead of main, issueId-linked conversation, gated partial-bead progress from a per-issue rollup, in_progress beads, recent spec activity) — all gated on GitHub-issue-OPEN so closed-orphan noise stays out. Feed the bead signals from a new rollup service that computes {total, closed, inProgress, lastUpdated} per issue from ONE bulk getAllBeads() call, refreshed on beads.freshness_changed (fixed to also fire on local writes). Let pan handoff declare/auto-detect an issue association (the issue_id column already exists end-to-end). Stop the leak at the source: sweep remaining open beads with a reason category at closeOut and postMergeLifecycle, add a one-shot pan beads sweep backfill for the 36 existing orphan carriers, and add an explicit no-open-beads check to the verification gate (fail-closed on timeout per PAN-1812). Surface stalled work (in-pipeline artifacts, no live agent, no recent activity) as its own Command Deck bucket.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No per-issue bd queries at render time; all bead signals come from the single bulk rollup (NFR).
- No persisted domain event carrying the derived rollup payload; the rollup is an in-memory service cache (D2).
- No new bead status value ('cancelled' stays a close reason, not a bd status; D5).
- No changes to the PAN-2054 terminal-issue exclusion: GitHub-closed issues (except open-PR) must never re-enter the tree, even with the new signals (AC-6).
- No auto-verification of WHAT orphaned beads represent during the sweep (done vs obsolete is carried as the close-reason text; the sweep does not re-audit functionality).
- No removal of the Conversations section: issue-nested conversations are additive (D7).
- No configuration surface for the 14-day recency window; it is a named constant.
- No changes to review convoy mechanics or done-preflight behavior (FR-4 adds a verification-gate check alongside, not instead).

autoDecisions.summary: Rollup cache is a dashboard-server in-memory service (not a read-model reducer field fed by a persisted event).
autoDecisions.rationale: Its only consumer is resource discovery in the same process; persisting a ~400-issue derived rollup to the append-only event store on every bead write would bloat the log with derivable data. The NFR's intent (O(1) at render, event-driven refresh, one bulk list) is fully met.

autoDecisions.summary: Recency window N = 14 days, hardcoded constant.
autoDecisions.rationale: Evidence: the two genuine stalled issues were ~51 days stale; 14 days separates active work from debris and adding config was not requested (simplicity-first).

autoDecisions.summary: beads.freshness_changed is fixed to fire on local writes by comparing against the previous poll's head, instead of adding a new write-door event.
autoDecisions.rationale: The NFR names 'the existing bead-write event'; the existing event's before/after-within-one-poll comparison provably misses local writes (beads-sync-service.ts:100-107). Fixing its detection is smaller and keeps one event type.

autoDecisions.summary: Merge-time sweep reason is 'issue merged; remaining open beads swept'; close-out derives 'completed' vs 'not planned' phrasing from the close context.
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue comment requires an honest per-bead reason category (done/obsolete/abandoned); at automated terminals the tracker close state is the only mechanical category source.

autoDecisions.summary: The stalled surface is a new Command Deck pipeline bucket in pipeline-helpers.ts, not a separate page.
autoDecisions.rationale: The needs-you grouping precedent (groupPipelineEntries) already re-buckets admitted issues; a bucket is the smallest change that surfaces the silent-drop set.

autoDecisions.summary: Backfill verb is `pan beads sweep` under the existing beads command group.
autoDecisions.rationale: It operates on beads and follows the mutate-through-writer pattern already in src/cli/commands/beads.ts; admin/db is for DB-plane rebuilds, not tracker-state reconciliation.

items.title: Fix beads.freshness_changed to fire on local writes (compare against previous poll head)

expected_outputs: beads-sync-service tests pass including a new case where a head change without a pull delta emits beads.freshness_changed
typecheck completes without errors

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/server/services/beads-sync-service.ts (syncOnce, lines ~95-107), the emit condition compares the head before and after `dolt pull` within one poll, so a local write via runMutationBatch (which advances the head before the poll) never fires beads.freshness_changed. Change the detection to compare the freshly observed head against the PREVIOUS poll's recorded head (track last-observed head per project, e.g. extend the healthByProject entry or the existing lastRemoteHead map): emit when observed != lastObserved, then record the new head. First poll (no previous head) records without emitting. Add/extend unit tests: (a) remote pull advances head → event emitted (existing behavior preserved); (b) head already advanced locally before poll, pull is a no-op → event NOW emitted; (c) no head movement → no event. Use fake timers for any interval logic per repo rule.

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/server/services/beads-rollup-service.ts: a per-project in-memory cache mapping lowercase issue label (e.g. 'pan-2602') → { total: number, closed: number, inProgress: number, lastUpdated: string | null } plus a per-project staleness flag. Compute from ONE createBeadsResolver(project.beadsCwd).getAllBeads() call (resolver at src/lib/beads/resolver.ts:104; the 64MB maxBuffer and shared lock are already handled there; use a generous acquisitionTimeoutMs of several seconds — the 500ms starvation bug was just fixed in commit 4f6db409ef). Group beads by issue label reusing labelMatchesIssue semantics from src/lib/beads-query.ts:106-111 (accept bare 'pan-N' and 'workspace:pan-N' forms; a bead may carry several labels — count it under each issue label it carries). closed = status==='closed', inProgress = status==='in_progress', lastUpdated = max(updated_at) across the issue's beads. On a failed read ({ok:false} BeadsReadResult), KEEP the previous rollup and mark the project stale — never replace with empty (PAN-1812, hazard H1). Refresh triggers: one compute at service start, then recompute on each beads.freshness_changed event for that projectKey (subscribe via the event store like domain-services.ts:170-177), debounced trailing-edge ~2s to absorb bursts. Export a synchronous getter getBeadRollups(projectKey) → { rollups: Map, stale: boolean } | null for resource discovery. Wire service start in src/dashboard/server/main.ts next to createBeadsSyncService (~line 489). Tests use vi.useFakeTimers() for the debounce per repo rule and mock the resolver.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/lifecycle/orphaned-beads-sweep.ts exporting async sweepOrphanedBeads(opts: { beadsCwd: string; issueId: string; reason: string; dryRun?: boolean }): Promise<SweepResult> where SweepResult = { ok: boolean; closedIds: string[]; skipped: number; error?: string }. Steps: (1) read the issue's beads via createBeadsResolver(opts.beadsCwd).getBeadsForIssue(issueId) (src/lib/beads/resolver.ts:82); on {ok:false} return { ok:false, error } and close NOTHING (PAN-1812 / H1 — a failed read is unknown, not zero). (2) Filter status 'open' or 'in_progress'. (3) If none, return ok with empty closedIds (idempotent — safe to re-run, H3). (4) Unless dryRun, close each via the canonical writer: runMutationBatch (src/lib/beads/writer.ts:87) with bd.mutate(['close', id, '--reason', opts.reason]) exactly as src/cli/commands/beads.ts:265 does — never raw bd (bd-shim blocks it). One runMutationBatch for the whole batch. (5) Return the report. No lifecycle events, no tracker writes — callers own context. Unit tests with mocked resolver/writer covering all four ACs.
